title: This Cranberry Brie Bread is the Only Reason I’m Surviving Tuesday
description: Ditch the extra dishes. This gooey, one-pan cranberry brie bread is the ultimate low-effort, high-reward comfort food for busy weeknights. Ready in 20 minutes.
story: Look, I love cooking, but I also love my couch and not spending my life scrubbing pans. After a ten-hour day, the last thing I want is a sink full of dishes. That’s why I’m obsessed with this cranberry brie bread. It’s basically a fancy appetizer that I’ve decided is a perfectly acceptable dinner. I toss everything into my trusty cast iron skillet, shove it in the oven, and call it a day. The first time I tried this, I used a soft sourdough that turned into a soggy mess; lesson learned—stick to a sturdier loaf like Trader Joe’s brioche or a rustic boule that can actually hold the weight of all that melted cheese. It’s warm, sweet, salty, and best of all, there’s literally one pan to clean. If you're a fellow dish-hater, this is going to be your new go-to when you just can't deal with a full meal prep.
ingredients: 1 round loaf of crusty sourdough or brioche (about 12 oz)
8 oz wheel of double-cream Brie, rind trimmed and cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 cup whole berry cranberry sauce (the canned stuff works fine here, no judgment)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F. Use a serrated knife to cut a grid pattern into the top of the bread, going about 3/4 of the way down without cutting through the bottom crust.
Stuff the cubes of Brie into the bread crevices. Don't worry if it looks messy; it's going to melt into a glorious, gooey disaster anyway.
Spoon the cranberry sauce into the gaps between the cheese. Brush the top of the bread with the melted butter and sprinkle with the rosemary and salt.
Place the loaf directly into your cast iron skillet. Bake for 14-16 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the bread edges are golden brown. Serve immediately while it's still molten.
proHack: Don't skip the rind trimming on the Brie. If you leave too much of it on, the cheese won't melt into that perfect liquid gold consistency, and you'll end up with rubbery chunks instead of a smooth dip.
storage: If you have leftovers (which is a miracle), wrap the bread in foil and store it in the fridge for up to two days. To reheat, pop the foil-wrapped loaf into a 350°F oven for about 8-10 minutes until the center is soft again. Don't microwave it unless you want rubbery bread.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the cranberry sauce if I don't have it?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Fig jam or even a spicy pepper jelly works beautifully if you want to swap the sweet-tart profile for something earthy or kicked-up.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the bread from burning?
faqs.answer: Keep an eye on it around the 12-minute mark. If the top of the bread is browning too fast but the cheese isn't melted, tent a small piece of foil loosely over the skillet.
